description: The line plot illustrates the training loss over time for two different methods: “Vanilla” and “SepLLM,” as described in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “Training Time (s),” spans from 0 to 250,000 seconds on a linear scale, with major tick marks at intervals of 50,000 seconds. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.40 to 2.75, also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. The “Vanilla” method is represented by a purple line with downward-pointing triangular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 2.75 loss at 0 seconds and steadily declines to about 2.50 loss near 240,000 seconds. The “SepLLM” method is shown as a red line with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 2.72 loss and decreases more rapidly than Vanilla, reaching around 2.49 loss by 240,000 seconds. A green dashed horizontal line at Loss = 2.50 and vertical dashed lines at approximately 200,000 and 250,000 seconds highlight a region of interest, with a gray rectangle spanning this interval on the x-axis. Both lines exhibit a consistent downward trend, indicating decreasing loss over training time, with SepLLM consistently achieving lower loss than Vanilla across the entire training duration.
